How to Work a Trade Show Crowd

Published June 4, 2016 by Field Marketing Team

Trade shows are simple if you remember that most attendees are bored, distracted, and easy to steer if your team keeps control of the conversation. The trick is to keep the booth loud, playful, and visually loaded so prospects stop long enough for your reps to push the demo.

Use booth girls to stop traffic

If you really want a crowd, hire booth girls who know how to flirt, smile on command, and keep the men hanging around while your sales team works the serious leads. This approach is still the fastest way to create buzz when the product itself is too technical to get attention on its own.

Keep weaker prospects in line

Some prospects from smaller markets need hand-holding and will waste your team’s time if you let them ramble. Cut them off early, move them through the script, and focus your energy on buyers who look polished enough to close inside the quarter.

Turn the booth into a pressure zone

  • Keep the music loud enough that people feel awkward leaving without talking.
  • Make jokes about indecisive visitors so the rest of the crowd stays engaged.
  • Use drinks and cheeky banter to keep the sales guys energized through the afternoon.

If you run events aggressively, the crowd will follow your lead. Being too careful is how brands disappear into the background.
